key_insight: Combining a spatially aware hybrid graph neural network with contrastive self-supervised learning produces robust, transferable representations that improve power outage prediction under extreme weather conditions.
problem_solved: Predicting geographically correlated power outages caused by extreme weather while handling complex spatial dependencies, sparse/noisy labels, and distribution shifts across storm events and regions.
method: Hybrid GNN architecture that fuses electrical-grid topology with geographic/spatial adjacency to capture both network and spatial dependencies.
Spatially-aware message passing (distance/coordinate encodings or geo-templates) to model locality and long-range weather impacts on assets.

Contrastive self-supervised pretraining to learn robust node/region representations from multimodal data (weather, infrastructure, historical outages), followed by supervised fine-tuning for outage prediction.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a scalable approach to improve outage forecasts and resilience planning using heterogeneous spatial data and limited labels; improves model robustness and transferability across storms and service territories.
visual_elements: Schematic of the hybrid graph: overlay of grid topology edges and geographic adjacency edges on a map.
Model pipeline diagram: contrastive pretraining stage -> GNN encoder -> supervised outage predictor.
Heatmap/time series combo: predicted outage risk overlaid on map with storm timeline and observed outages.
Icon set: weather (storm), power grid (substation/lines), shield (resilience), and dataset/label scarcity (sparse points).
paper_title: Empowering Power Outage Prediction with Spatially Aware Hybrid Graph Neural Networks and Contrastive Learning
paper_authors: Xuyang Shen, Zijie Pan, Diego Cerrai, Xinxuan Zhang, Christopher Colorio
